models.name: Claude Fable 5.1
models.role: Demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work
strengths: Anthropic's pick when evals on Opus 5.5 at higher effort still fall short
Adaptive thinking is always on and defaults to high effort, so hard problems get budget without prompting for it
Holds a plan together across very long agentic runs
weaknesses: The most expensive model in the family at 2.5x Opus 5.5 per token, and slower to first output
Overkill for routine work: Opus 5.5 matches it on most tasks for less
OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol claims comparable results on agentic coding at a fifth of the price, so it is worth benchmarking on your own workload

models.name: Claude Opus 5.5
models.role: Long-running agentic coding and knowledge work
strengths: The default recommendation for most workloads: Fable-level results on most work at a lower price
Cache reads at $0.20/MTok make long agentic sessions, where cached context dominates the bill, much cheaper
Adaptive thinking always on, with effort tunable from low to max
weaknesses: Moderate latency: not the one for interactive, token-by-token UX
Still 2x Sonnet 5.5 per token, and Sonnet 5.5 is close enough on many tasks that the gap has to be measured, not assumed

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5.5
models.role: The best combination of speed and intelligence
strengths: Fast with a 1M context window, which is the combination most product work actually needs
Defaults to high effort, so quality does not depend on remembering to raise it
Needs fewer tokens than Sonnet 5 for the same work, so cost per task drops even at identical token prices
weaknesses: Thinking is adaptive rather than always on, so the hardest problems need the effort level raised deliberately
Falls behind Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 on the longest agentic runs

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
strengths: The fastest Claude, and the cheapest, for classification, extraction and high-volume calls
Near-frontier quality for its tier at a fifth of Opus 5.5's token price
weaknesses: Knowledge cutoff of Feb 2025 is well over a year behind the 5.5 family's Jun 2026
200K context and 64K output, a fifth of the rest of the family
The oldest model listed here and scheduled for retirement no sooner than Oct 15, 2026; Haiku 5.5 was announced as joining the 5.5 family, so check for it before building on this one

models.name: GPT-6 Astra
models.role: OpenAI's most capable model for the most demanding work
strengths: OpenAI's flagship for complex reasoning and coding, and their strongest computer-use model
Effort levels run from low all the way to max, so one model covers a wide cost/quality range
Better than its predecessors at making a sensible call when instructions leave room for interpretation
weaknesses: Priced like Fable 5.1 at $10/$50, the most expensive option on this page
GPT-6.1 Sol reaches near-Astra quality at a fifth of the price, which makes Astra hard to justify outside the hardest work
Knowledge cutoff Apr 30, 2026

models.name: GPT-6.1 Sol
models.role: Near-Astra performance for complex work at a lower cost
strengths: Nearly matches Astra on agentic coding, computer use and professional work at a fifth of its token price
Fewer factual errors than GPT-6 Sol and more reliable at respecting explicit restrictions during agentic tasks
A `pro` reasoning mode is available for hard problems without switching models
weaknesses: `pro` mode spends far more reasoning tokens, costing several times a normal request and taking much longer — not for everyday work
Not available in ChatGPT's Chat surface at launch (Work and Codex only), so behaviour there can differ from the API
Knowledge cutoff Apr 30, 2026

models.name: GPT-6 Luna
models.role: Most efficient model for focused, high-volume tasks
strengths: By far the cheapest hosted model here, 20x cheaper than Sol on input, and it keeps the full 1.05M context
Reasoning effort can be set to `none`, which no other model on this page allows, for latency-critical calls
Newest knowledge cutoff of the hosted models at May 18, 2026
weaknesses: Built for focused tasks: it is the weakest hosted model here on open-ended reasoning and long agentic runs
Cheap tokens plus a 1M window invites stuffing context that it will not use as well as a larger model would

models.name: Gemma 4
models.role: Google's open-weight multimodal family, frontier-level at each size
models.context: Varies by tag; Ollama defaults the window far lower
strengths: Vision, audio, tool calling and thinking in one open-weight family, which is rare locally
The size ladder reaches from a 2B laptop build to 31B, so the same prompts scale with hardware
The most actively updated family in the Ollama library
weaknesses: The 26B and 31B builds need a 24 GB-class GPU at 4-bit quantization
Quantized local builds lose quality against the hosted originals in ways benchmarks do not always show
Multimodal input costs context fast, and local context windows are much tighter than the 1M hosted ones

models.name: Qwen 3.5
models.role: Alibaba's open multimodal family with the widest size ladder
models.context: Varies by tag; Ollama defaults the window far lower
strengths: Seven sizes from 0.8B to 122B: the easiest family to match to whatever hardware you actually have
Vision, tool calling and thinking across the range
Strong multilingual coverage, which the Llama builds are weaker at
weaknesses: The 122B tag is out of reach for a single consumer GPU
Tool-calling reliability under long agentic loops still trails the hosted frontier models
Fast-moving release cadence means tutorials and Modelfiles go stale quickly

models.name: gpt-oss
models.role: OpenAI's open-weight models for reasoning and agentic use
models.context: Varies by tag; Ollama defaults the window far lower
strengths: Adjustable reasoning effort locally, which most open-weight models do not expose
The 20B build fits a 16 GB card at 4-bit quantization, making it the practical pick for one mid-range GPU
Built for tool use and agentic loops rather than chat alone
weaknesses: Only two sizes, so there is nothing between a 16 GB build and a 120B one
Not updated in about a year — the Gemma 4 and Qwen 3.5 families have moved on since
Shares a name and lineage with OpenAI's hosted models but not their quality; do not treat it as a local GPT-6

models.name: Qwen3-Coder
models.role: Long-context open model aimed at agentic coding
models.context: Long-context by local standards; raise `num_ctx` to use it
strengths: Purpose-built for agentic coding rather than general chat
The 30B build is the usual choice for a 24 GB card and keeps a long window at small-model speed
A credible local option for code that must not leave the machine
weaknesses: Coding-specialised, so it is a poor general assistant
The 480B tag is server hardware, not homelab hardware
Well behind Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol on long multi-file changes

models.name: DeepSeek-R1
models.context: Varies by tag; Ollama defaults the window far lower
strengths: The open model that made visible chain-of-thought reasoning normal, and still a reference point for it
The widest size range in the library, including distills that run on a laptop
Thinking and tool tags across the family
weaknesses: About a year old: the 2026 families beat it at equivalent sizes
The small distills carry the reasoning style without much of the reasoning ability
Thinking output is verbose, which eats a local context window quickly

models.name: Llama 3.1
models.role: Meta's workhorse, still the most-pulled model in the library
models.context: Varies by tag; Ollama defaults the window far lower
strengths: The widest ecosystem support of any local model: nearly every tool, tutorial and Modelfile assumes it works
The 8B build runs on an 8 GB card and is the safe default for a first local setup
Reliable tool calling for its age
weaknesses: Over a year old and clearly behind Gemma 4 and Qwen 3.5 at the same sizes
Text only — no vision, no audio
Its popularity reflects tutorial inertia rather than current quality; pick it for compatibility, not capability
